title: ServiceTitan alternatives for small contractors
summary: Find the best ServiceTitan alternative for your trade business. We compare 8 tools for small crews based on pricing, features, strengths, and drawbacks.
body_markdown:
## Overview


ServiceTitan can do a lot. For a small shop, that can also mean a lot to pay for, set up, and learn.


If you’re an owner-operator or running a small crew, the best tool for you depends on the areas of the business where you need more help. Maybe you need more leads, or maybe estimates and invoices are eating up your evenings. Maybe you’re adding techs and need a way to keep the schedule straight.


The point is, different ServiceTitan competitors are built for different aspects of the job.


Below, we’ll compare the best options, who each is most suited for, and what real users say.


## Topline Pro


Topline Pro’s platform uses Sidekick, its proprietary AI system, to build a custom website designed with built-in SEO and GEO (generative engine optimization). That way, your business appears on traditional search engines like Google and AI tools like ChatGPT. Sidekick also writes and publishes search-friendly blog posts and social media updates regularly to keep your site dynamic and signal authority to search engines.


A unique feature of Topline Pro websites is the platform’s Showcases feature. With Showcases, you upload a few photos and a quick description via text or the app, and the system auto-builds a polished presentation. You can attach real 5-star customer feedback directly to the project to build instant social proof. Each showcase includes an integrated booking form so prospective clients can easily request a quote for similar local work.


Topline Pro users don’t simply have to sit back and passively wait for inquiries to come in, though. They can use Prospect Feed to pounce on local leads in real time. Prospect Feed scans local community platforms like Nextdoor daily to find homeowners in your service area who are asking for specific home services.


While you are out in the field doing physical work, Sidekick can be set up to do things like answer inbound calls, qualify new leads, and track prospects through your pipeline.


Sidekick will also turn rough job notes into clean, branded digital quotes, featuring your logo and complete with custom line items and contract terms. It notifies you when homeowners open or accept quotes and generates professional invoices once the work is done.


### Best for


Topline Pro is best for contractors ready to grow past the “word-of-mouth” marketing stage without hiring separate marketing, sales, and office help.


Pros like[Thelma Zuniga](https://share.google/rTO8eoDl4W37uBsHr) of City Wide Roofing praise Topline Pro as a “one-stop shop” for creating your website, managing your social feed, and shipping quotes, invoices, and review requests.


“It is exactly what our business needed to function at its best,” Zuniga said.


### Drawbacks


Some reviewers wanted faster lead results, but overall, Topline Pro’s 400+ Google reviews are overwhelmingly positive.


### Pricing


- **Starter Plan** $199/month
- **Core Plan** $249/month
- **Pro Plan** $299/month


## Housecall Pro


Housecall Pro is an all-in-one field service management software. It stands out for its deep set of dispatching tools.


Once customers choose a service and available time, Housecall Pro’s visual calendar gives the office a clear view of who’s available.


Dispatchers can drag and drop jobs between technicians, track tech locations with GPS, and see estimated travel times. Technicians use the mobile app to clock in and out, track travel time, and record how long they spend on each job. Managers can review and edit those time entries, and approved hours can sync with payroll tools.


Housecall Pro also offers AI tools for answering calls, booking jobs, creating invoices, and pulling plain-English reports on revenue, job trends, and average ticket size.


### Best for


Housecall Pro fits the bill for small service businesses with multiple techs and a busy daily schedule that need strong dispatching tools to keep jobs, routes, and field crews organized.


### Drawbacks


Reviewers generally like Housecall Pro’s ease of use, but some report mobile-app issues or unintuitive workflows.


Other reviewers mention being surprised by having to pay more for new features and additional services, and Housecall Pro confirms that add-ons and users beyond those included in a plan can cost extra.


### Pricing


- ‍ **‍** No public pricing available. You must engage Service Fusion’s sales team to get a quote.


## Jobber


Jobber offers a clean, beginner-friendly design and streamlined dashboard that helps small field service teams get up and running in just days.


You can build quotes from your phone or computer, pull in saved services and pricing, request deposits, and send estimates by text or email. Customers approve through Jobber’s Client Hub, and once they say yes, the quote can be turned into a job without re-entering all the details.


Customers can book online based on your team’s availability, while the calendar and map help you see who’s assigned where. Jobber can optimize routes to cut down on backtracking. Field crews can also track time, upload photos, complete checklists, and add job notes from the mobile app.


Jobber goes deeper on the business side as you move up pricing plans. Job costing tracks labor, materials, and expenses against each job, while Pipeline lets you move leads through custom sales stages and flag opportunities that have gone quiet. Client profiles keep quotes, jobs, invoices, payments, notes, and customer communications together in one history.


Jobber can build a marketing plan from the jobs and customers already in your account, then draft emails, social posts, review requests, and job showcases for you to approve. Its website, Google Business Profile tools, and online booking are designed to turn that work into new and repeat business.


### Best for


Small service businesses moving away from paper, spreadsheets, or a collection of basic tools and looking for one straightforward system to manage customers and jobs.


### Drawbacks


Some reviewers say the mobile app still has fewer options than the desktop version. One[2026 reviewer](https://www.g2.com/products/jobber/reviews?filters%5Bcomment_answer_values%5D=&order=most_recent&page=5#:~:text=They%20also%20attempted%20to%20roll%20out%20a%20pipeline%2C%20but%20it%E2%80%99s%20only%20for%20quotes%2C%20and%20they%20decided%20to%20charge%20extra%20for%20it%20after%20the%20beta.%20It%20still%20isn%E2%80%99t%20available%20on%20phones.) , for example, wanted to handle pipeline on mobile rather than having to use a computer.


Others say Jobber’s reporting is too basic for their needs.


Pricing can also climb as your team grows or you need more advanced tools. Features such as job costing, more advanced automations, Pipeline, Marketing Tools, and AI Receptionist sit on higher plans or add-ons rather than the entry-level tier.


### Pricing


- Depends on team size. Check out their website for a tool that shows you the price you’ll pay based on your precise number of users.


## FieldPulse


FieldPulse focuses on big companies that want to standardize work across a large roster of field techs.


The platform’s ClearPath tool lets you build different workflows for different types of jobs. At each stage, you can require technicians to complete certain forms, upload photos, or take specific actions before moving on. Techs see a simplified Focus View in the mobile app that walks them through the next steps instead of showing them every option in the system.


Number crunchers love FieldPulse because you can create custom dashboards that cover technician performance, revenue, expenses, job profitability, and other operational metrics.


FieldPulse also goes deeper than many small-business field-service tools on inventory and equipment management. You can track parts across warehouses, trucks, and job sites, move stock between locations, monitor serialized equipment, and tie materials back to work orders. Its asset tools keep records on both company and customer equipment, including installation dates, warranties, condition, and service history.


### Best for


FieldPulse is particularly well-suited to larger shops managing a lot of parts, equipment, or repeat service work, such as HVAC, plumbing, electrical, commercial equipment, and other trades where technicians need detailed job steps and equipment history in the field.


Customization is a recurring theme in recent reviews. One specialty roofing company on[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/fieldpulse-fieldpulse/reviews#:~:text=It%20is%20the%20next%20best%20thing%20to%20proprietary%20software%20(which%20would%20be%20way%20out%20of%20our%20budget)%2C%20because%20FieldPulse%20is%20highly%20customizable%20for%20different%20ways%20of%20running%20a%20business.%20Integrating%20with%20Quickbooks%20is%20the%20icing%20on%20the%20cake.) described FieldPulse as “the next best thing to proprietary software” because of how closely they could tailor it to their operation.


### Drawbacks


All that flexibility can also create more setup and complexity.


Some reviewers say there are so many options that finding the right information can take several steps. A March 2026[G2 reviewer](https://www.g2.com/products/fieldpulse-fieldpulse/reviews/fieldpulse-review-12447912#:~:text=I%20often%20forget%20how%20to%20find%20what%20I%20need%20on%20a%20work%20order%20because%20it%20takes%20multiple%20steps%20to%20get%20to%20the%20right%20place%2C%20and%20it%E2%80%99s%20not%20always%20clear%20where%20to%20go%20next.%20There%20is%20so%20much%20the%20software%20offers%2C%20that%20it%20can%20get%20in%20the%20way.) said the amount the software offers can sometimes “get in the way,” while an April 2026[Capterra reviewer](https://www.capterra.com/p/153475/FieldPulse/reviews/) described having to jump between different parts of the system to find everything connected to a job.


Other reviewers report occasional bugs, mobile-app issues, or problems with QuickBooks syncing. Experiences vary — FieldPulse still holds strong overall ratings on both G2 and Capterra — but those are worth asking about during a demo if your shop depends heavily on mobile access or accounting integrations.


### Pricing


- Pricing is user-based, but no public pricing is available. You must talk to FieldPulse’s sales team to get a quote.


## Service Fusion


Like Housecall Pro, Service Fusion leans heavily into its GPS tools, so dispatchers can better track their reps in the field.


Office staff can use the Dispatch Grid to see technicians and jobs across a time-based schedule, then drag unscheduled work into an open slot. Techs receive assignments in the mobile app and update statuses such as On The Way, On Site, Started, and Completed, giving the office a live view of what’s happening in the field.


Service Fusion also offers GPS fleet tracking for shops that want more visibility into their trucks. With the optional hardware installed, managers can see vehicle locations, trip history, drive and idle time, and alerts for things like speeding or harsh braking.


Techs can use the mobile app to access customer and service history, add job photos, build estimates, invoice, and take payment in the field.


### Best for


Shops that are adding employees quickly will love Service Fusion’s unlimited users pricing, because it means their bill won’t jump every time a new person needs a login.


### Drawbacks


Several useful features also require a higher plan or add-on. On Starter, inventory management, job costing, GPS fleet tracking, customer portals, and ServiceCall.ai all cost extra.


Reviewers also point to limitations in the mobile app and reporting. One January[2026 Capterra reviewer](https://www.capterra.com/p/135788/Service-Fusion/reviews) said senior team members often need a laptop because “far too many functions” aren’t available in the field app. Another April 2026 reviewer said the reporting didn’t let her get the job and service-plan information her company needed.


### Pricing


- No public pricing available. You must engage Service Fusion’s sales team to get a quote.


## Projul


Projul is for contractors running multi-day or multi-week projects, rather than shops knocking out a string of short service calls.


Its scheduling tools are the clearest example of where it stands out. On the Core+ plan, you can lay a project out on a Gantt chart or linear timeline, turn estimate items into project tasks, and shift an entire timeline when one delay pushes everything else back. That makes it easier to see how framing, electrical, drywall, finish work, and subcontractors fit together.


Job costing and budgeting let you track project costs as work progresses, while progress billing and change orders help manage jobs where the final invoice isn’t simply sent after one visit. The client portal gives homeowners or project owners a place to see schedules, messages, photos, approvals, and other project updates.


For crews in the field, Projul’s higher-tier plan adds geofenced time tracking, where the system can flag clock-ins that happen outside the job-site area. That gives the office a better picture of labor going into each project and makes it easier to tie those hours back to job costs.


### Best for


Projul is specifically for remodelers, general contractors, builders, and specialty contractors managing longer jobs with multiple stages, crews, or subcontractors.


A November 2025[G2 reviewer](https://www.g2.com/products/projul/reviews) running renovation and new-build projects praised Projul for keeping subcontractor scheduling and budgets together, saying it helped them manage projects “from start to finish.”


### Drawbacks


Projul is a much bigger upfront commitment than most of the small-contractor tools on this list. The entry plan starts at $4,788 per year. However, features that make Projul particularly useful for complex projects, like Gantt charts, job costing, change orders, the client portal, and progress billing, require the $7,188-per-year Core+ plan.


### Pricing


- ‍ **Core** $4,788/annually **‍**
- **Core+** $7,188/annually **‍**
- **Pro** $14,388/annually


## Workiz


The most distinctive feature of Workiz is its “Genius” AI-powered scheduling tool.


When a new job comes in, Genius Scheduling suggests the best technician and time slot based on availability, skills, and how close that job is to other appointments already on the calendar. It also accounts for job duration and travel time, which helps dispatchers avoid unrealistic back-to-back bookings and reduce unnecessary driving.


The rest of the Genius suite tackles other front-office work. Genius Answering acts as a 24/7 receptionist that can answer calls and messages, respond to common questions, and book jobs into the schedule. Genius Leads turns incoming service requests into leads without someone re-entering the details, while Smart Messaging helps draft customer texts and emails based on the conversation and job history. Call Insights can transcribe calls, summarize them, and flag possible upsell opportunities.


Workiz also handles the usual field-service workflow around those tools, including estimates, jobs, customer records, invoicing, payments, and technician scheduling.


### Best for


Workiz is most useful for shops where scheduling has become too complicated to manage by eyeballing the calendar.


Instead of manually checking which tech is free, who has the right skills, and whether they can realistically get across town in time, the system surfaces options for the dispatcher to choose from.


### Drawbacks


Some of Workiz’s most distinctive tools aren’t part of the basic package. Genius Answering and other Genius products may require higher plans or additional fees, so the cost can climb if you want the full front-office automation setup.


Some reviewers also complain about[add-on costs](https://www.g2.com/products/workiz/reviews) , contract terms, and occasional mobile or scheduling issues.


### Pricing


- No public pricing available. You must engage Workiz’s sales team to get a quote.


## Rebolt


Rebolt tries to make life easier for the owner wearing many hats by streamlining that miles-long to-do list down to the most urgent tasks.


Instead of making you dig through different screens to find what needs attention, its “Catch Up” feature gives you a swipeable queue of new leads, pending quotes, overdue invoices, and upcoming jobs.


Rebolt also offers voice-to-quote. You can describe the work out loud and have Rebolt build a quote, then pull items from your price book, send it for online approval, and follow up if the customer hasn’t signed.


Like other tools, Rebolt offers an optional AI Voice Assistant to answer incoming calls, collect lead information, qualify the request, and feed that information back into the CRM so the business can follow up or schedule the work.


Rebolt’s “Marketing Kit” includes an SEO-focused website, Google Business Profile optimization, social posting, review requests, and local project pages. A contractor can upload photos and details from a completed job, then publish them to Facebook, Instagram, Google Business Profile, and a geo-tagged project page on the website.


### Best for


Small home-service businesses who don’t want to spend their day bouncing between a scheduling app, website company, social tools, review software, and lead inbox.


### Drawbacks


Rebolt is newer than Jobber, Housecall Pro, or Service Fusion, so there’s much less independent customer feedback to work with, and the feedback that has come in is shaky. Its iPhone app currently shows 20 ratings and a 3.8/5 average.


Rebolt’s Pricebook is currently desktop-only, as is the Payments section of Rebolt Pay.


And although Rebolt emphasizes simple pricing, the Voice Agent is a separate add-on rather than part of the standard CRM or full platform price.


### Pricing


- ‍ **CRM** $99/month **‍**
- **Marketing Kit** $299/month **‍**
- **Full Platform** $349/month
- **Add On:** **Voice Agent** $99/month
